entities.summary:
Count Hans Meinhard von Schönberg auf Wesel was a German nobleman and soldier, who served as hofmeister of Frederick V, Elector Palatine.

Born on August 28, 1582, in Bacharach, a small town in the Electorate of the Palatinate, von Schönberg came from a prominent family of administrators and military leaders. His early life was marked by a strong sense of duty and loyalty to the Palatine cause, which would shape his future decisions.

Von Schönberg's most notable achievement was his service as hofmeister to Frederick V, Elector Palatine, a position that allowed him to wield significant influence over the Palatine court and military. This appointment was a testament to the Palatine Elector's trust in von Schönberg's abilities and his commitment to the Palatine cause.

Despite his significant role in the Palatine court, von Schönberg's life was cut short when he died on August 3, 1616, at the age of 33. His early death marked a significant loss for the Palatine cause, and his legacy would be remembered for generations to come.

Von Schönberg's legacy is still felt today, and his story serves as a reminder of the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the early modern era. His life and career offer a fascinating glimpse into the world of 17th-century German politics and society, and his legacy continues to inspire historical study and debate.

In conclusion, Count Hans Meinhard von Schönberg auf Wesel was a significant figure in the history of the Palatine Electorate, and his story offers a valuable insight into the complexities of early modern German politics and society.
